description: CROSS-CUTTING: the defect is invisible to any single reviewer in isolation. The insurance certificate is valid, ample and unexpired - it covers Great Britain only. The delivery model is direct-to-store and the store list includes Belfast and Londonderry, which are outside that cover. Neither document is wrong on its own; the defect exists only in the JOIN. This is the case where the isolation that prevents anchoring should also prevent the join, so multi-agent is PREDICTED TO LOSE here - the single agent sees both documents in one context.

expected.note: Cover is Great Britain only; the agreed delivery list includes Belfast and Londonderry, which are in Northern Ireland and therefore outside it. Every number on the certificate passes and the policy is in force - the amount is ample, the dates are valid. The defect is the mismatch between two documents that are each individually correct, and the two documents belong to two different reviewers. Scored against FINANCE because the territorial limit is a finance-area check, but a finding from LOGISTICS naming the same mismatch is equally correct and the harness counts it as routed to the wrong area rather than missed.
